business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Grocery Store Retailing of Imported Asian Condiments and Veg

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary National Jurisdiction, No Sub-Tax Distinctions)

Benelux Economic Union investment policy framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS Law), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract from Foreign Commercial Register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registrar of Companies in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority; if country of origin is not a Hague Convention member, Luxembourg Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Existence Certificate of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registrar of Companies or Tax Authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization through the relevant Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copy or National Identity Document of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner and Manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Authority / Civil Registry of the country of origin, with notarization by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notary attestation or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn translation into French/German/Luxembourgish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney executed by foreign shareholders in favor of the Luxembourg incorporation counsel or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin, or competent consular authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with sworn translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Registered Corporate Seat and Operational Address (utility bill, lease, or tax attestation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, landlord, or competent tax authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the certified copy, plus sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against: EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; Luxembourg Ministry of Finance Targeted Financial Sanctions List; OFAC SDN List for cross-border banking and US-dollar exposure; FATF Public Statements and High-Risk Jurisdictions List; CSSF administrative sanctions and PEP database. Positive hits must be escalated to senior management and reported to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) where suspicious activity is identified; all negative screening evidence must be preserved as part of the incorporation KYC file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in French, German, or Luxembourgish, or in a Latin-script transliteration of those languages; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name; the corporate suffix 'S.A.R.L.' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' must appear in the statutory form; the name must not imply a public-law entity, sovereign link, or regulated banking/insurance activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the 30-day validity window, the future shareholder must file the incorporatation deed with the RCS; if the name is not used, a new reservation request may be filed before expiry to obtain a fresh reservation. Upon a formal name-rejection decision issued by the RCS through LBR, the applicant may lodge a written administrative appeal before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification, stating the RCS case identifier and the grounds of abuse/error in the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office for an ISIC 4721 physical grocery retail operation; the company must maintain a verifiable physical retail and storage address in Luxembourg. Virtual administrative mail-handling services may be used only as an ancillary correspondence facility, not as the registered seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 8% annualized probability for a low-risk, non-cash-intensive specialty grocery retail store; the risk may rise to 15-20% if the UBO structure involves non-resident PEPs, large cash transactions, or anomalies identified in the mandatory AML/CFT risk assessment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 180-1 to 191 governing the société à responsabilité limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the electronic collection of companies and associations (RESA); Law of 15 March 2023 modernising commercial company law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with electronic lodgement via the notary and the guichet.lu single administrative portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution and statuts) deposited with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is EUR 12,400 under Article 180-1 of the 1915 Law; every share must be fully subscribed; at least 25% of cash contributions (EUR 3,100) must be paid up at incorporation and non-cash contributions paid up in full; payment is evidenced by a Luxembourg bank certificate of deposit, and no statutory public escrow is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTIONS OF THE MANAGER OF ASIAN SUPERMARKET GROCERY HUB, société à responsabilité limitée. The sole founding shareholder, having subscribed in full to the EUR 12,400 authorised share capital of the Company at formation, resolves as follows: (1) the share subscriptions, call payments and bank certificate of deposit are confirmed and entered in the minutes; (2) the registered office is adopted at [street address, Luxembourg City], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) [Name Surname], [nationality], is appointed manager (gérant) empowered to represent the Company, open bank accounts and contract in its name; (4) the manager is instructed to complete RCS registration, VAT and business-establishment filings, and all ancillary formalities. All resolutions are adopted unanimously and take immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Negative Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS via the guichet.lu portal and rcs.lu database search.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-search on the RCS electronic register for the proposed name ASIAN SUPERMARKET GROCERY HUB SARL; submit a formal request for confirmation that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing trade name; obtain the non-usage confirmation, which serves as the name reservation for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Passport or national ID of proposed manager(s)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the name due to confusing similarity, file a letter of consent from the prior-name holder or resubmit with up to three alternative names; a new negative certificate is processed within the same SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Deposit Bank Account and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in Luxembourg (e.g. BIL, Spuerkeess, BGL BNP Paribas, ING Luxembourg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated capital-deposit account in the name of the future SARL; complete full KYC/AML due diligence on the shareholders and source of funds; deposit at least EUR 3,100 (25% of the EUR 12,400 minimum capital) or the stated higher paid-up amount; instruct the bank to issue the attestation de blocage / certificate of deposit addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of address of each shareholder
Draft articles of association (statuts)
Business plan and AML source-of-funds declaration
Bank KYC questionnaire and reference letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of wealth, provide payroll slips, asset sale deeds or notarised shareholder affidavits; if the bank rejects the file, select another Luxembourg regulated bank and repeat the deposit; the capital remains blocked until RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the bank deposit certificate, negative name certificate, proof of identities and, where required, legalised powers of attorney to the notary; the notary drafts and reads the statuts covering the corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, share capital, share subscription table, duration, managers and permitted object; all shareholders or their attorneys appear and sign the deed before the notary, who authenticates it.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the capital deposit certificate
RCS name-availability confirmation
Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Original power of attorney and notarised translation if signed abroad
Tax residence certificate of corporate shareholders
UBO declaration data of each ultimate owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing annexes or a stale (>3 months old) bank certificate, obtain a refreshed certificate and execute a corrective addendum (acte rectificatif) before the same notary, then refile the complete deed with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via the electronic RCS platform filed by the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically transmits the authenticated deed of incorporation together with the statutory filing sheet (Formulaire A/B); the state fees (EUR 75 RCS filing fee and EUR 100 RESA publication fee) are settled; the RCS examines the file, issues the certificate of registration (extrait RCS) and arranges publication in the RESA, which gives the incorporation legal effectiveness against third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
RCS e-filing form signed by the notary
Proof of capital deposit
Power of attorney to the notary
Statement of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query on statutory clauses or annexes, the notary submits an explanatory brief or an amending deed within 15 days; once cured, the RCS completes registration and the RESA publication is backdated to the original deposit date if no third-party conflict arises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with the Social Security Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL as an employer with the CCSS before the first employee starts work and within eight days of the first hire; file the company data and manager identity details; obtain the CCSS employer identification number and enrol for employee registration and accident insurance.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Articles of incorporation
Identity documents of managers
Planned employment date and details of first employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS flags a late or incomplete employer declaration, submit a late-affiliation rectification letter with proof of the actual hiring date and pay any modest administrative surcharge; CCSS numbers are issued retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration with the Luxembourg Indirect Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic VAT registration application following the RCS certificate; provide the seat address, business activity code (ISIC 4721), manager identification and VAT-liability start date; the AEDT allocates a Luxembourg VAT number (LU prefix) and issues the periodic filing schedule, normally monthly or quarterly, with standard VAT returns through MyGuichet.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Identity document of the authorised signatory
Lease deed or proof of registered office
Bank details of the SARL
VAT registration form (Formulaire 904)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays issuance or requests additional evidence of the effective start of activity, file a reminder with a sworn accountant's statement and obtain the VAT number retroactive to the registration date; a formal spontaneous-registration procedure is available if a deadline has been missed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration in the RBE Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 calendar days of RCS registration, file the ultimate beneficial owner(s) holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights in the RBE electronic register; upload the identity data of each beneficial owner and appoint an authorised person for future updates; confirm the status as a market-convention retail grocery company subject to standard AML diligence by the LBR.
required_dossiers: RBE electronic filing form
Identity documents of each ultimate beneficial owner
RCS registration extract
Declaration of the nature of beneficial ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE rejects incomplete declarations, correct and resubmit online before expiry of the 30-day window; administrative fines for late filing are mitigated by filing a rectification declaration within 15 days of a notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, acting through the Service des Autorisations d'Établissement on the guichet.lu portal, in conjunction with the municipality (Ville de Luxembourg) for commercial location approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) for grocery retail under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craft, commercial and industrial business, supplemented by a food business operator registration with the Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) under the Ministry for the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier C — Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; the small-scale grocery retail project stays below the Annex II thresholds of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment and requires only a municipal building permit, food-hygiene registration and, where applicable, a wastewater discharge agreement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to public sewers must comply with the Law of 19 December 2008 on water and the municipal sewer by-laws; food waste and organic waste handling follows the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; refrigeration equipment must meet the F-gas leak-detection and recovery obligations of Regulation (EU) No 517/2014; VOC and odour emissions are limited to the thresholds of the municipal environmental code; packaging waste must conform to the extended producer responsibility rules of the Law of 17 July 2020; ambient noise levels must respect municipal nuisance limits at the boundary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by the municipal mayor after advice of the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), covering evacuation routes, extinguishers, and automatic detection in the retail sales area; structural load verification by the municipal building service for storage mezzanines; electrical installation conformity certificate from an accredited control body under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2015; workplace occupational clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering aisle safety, manual handling, staff rest areas, first-aid equipment and the sanitary conditions of the supermarket premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and EORI; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for commercial registration; digital portal: MyGuichet (myguichet.lu) and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SARL is constituted by notarial deed and entered in the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), which issues the national legal-entity identification number (numéro d'immatriculation / RCS number). For VAT, a distinct Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) is obtained by filing the VAT registration e-form (Formulaire 1022 / E-Form 'VAT registration') with the AEDT through MyGuichet, attaching the notarial deed, articles of association, a recent RCS extract, proof of a Luxembourg seat and economic activity, director identification, and intended business scope. Non-resident entities carrying on taxable supplies in Luxembourg or importing goods must complete the same AEDT procedure, appointing a tax representative where they are established outside the EU and outside any relevant mutual-assistance treaty; an EORI number must concurrently be obtained from the Administration des douanes et accises for customs import and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style 'check-the-box' mechanism; the SARL is mandatorily an entity-level corporate taxpayer. Available statutory elections include: (i) waiver of the small-business VAT franchise (voluntary VAT registration despite turnover below the EUR 35,000 exemption ceiling); (ii) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax purposes under Article 164bis LIR; (iii) option to apply VAT to lettings of immovable property; (iv) election of treatment under specific holding-company or investment-fund regimes where eligible; and (v) structuring hybrid instruments remains subject to the ATAD/anti-hybrid mismatch disallowance rules, which do not permit elective opt-out or mismatch passporting.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA), governed by the Loi TVA of 12 February 1979 as amended and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-business franchise exemption for Luxembourg-established taxable persons; non-established foreign suppliers and importers of goods are registrable without any turnover threshold; intra-EU cross-border B2C distance sales are subject to the EUR 10,000 Union OSS threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not implemented continuous transaction controls (CTC) or mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital invoicing for domestic B2B/B2C transactions; e-invoicing remains voluntary and PDF/paper invoices are accepted. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies to supplies to Luxembourg public-sector bodies via the PEPPOL network. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) directive will impose obligatory e-invoicing and digital reporting in the 2030-2035 horizon, with Luxembourg transposition legislation pending; exporters must meanwhile maintain machine-readable electronic export records consistent with the national NCTS/ECS customs systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU qualify for VAT zero-rating (exemption with credit) under Article 146(1)(a) of EU Directive 2006/112/EC and Article 57(1) Loi TVA, provided the supplier can produce conclusive evidence that the goods left the EU within the statutory export period (normally three months from supply) and were not processed or consumed before departure. The imported Asian condiments, preserved foods and vegetables qualify for 0% only when exported onward as commercial goods; intra-EU movements to other Member States are not zero-rated exports and must be reported as exempt intra-Community dispatches through VIES/ICL. Offshore B2B services (transport, logistics, brokerage, overseas storage) are zero-rated when the recipient belongs in a third country, subject to the Article 44 B2B place-of-supply rule. Domestic retail sales of groceries to Luxembourg consumers are subject to the applicable Luxembourg VAT scale (3% super-reduced, 8% reduced, 14% intermediate, or 16% standard rate depending on product category under Annexes A/B of the Loi TVA). Although Luxembourg imposes no statutory foreign-exchange control deadline, banking and administrative audit norms expect export proceeds to be received within 180 days of dispatch; longer settlement periods require documented commercial credit arrangements, and an Inward Remittance Certificate is maintained within that window to corroborate the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) bearing the electronic exit certification of the Administration des douanes et accises (NCTS/ECS system)
Original commercial invoice or proforma with packing list, stating the destination country and consideration
International transport document: CMR waybill, bill of lading, sea waybill, or air waybill evidencing physical movement to a third-country destination
NCTS/ECS transit and exit confirmation, or customs office departure/exit stamp trace
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103/ASR, or bank credit evidence of settlement received from the non-EU customer matching invoice value
Export order, customer acceptance, and freight-forwarder export declaration or third-country delivery evidence where an indirect export route is used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow zero-rating where the export proof package is incomplete, contradictory, or not produced within the statutory retention period (business records 10 years; assessment generally 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or false declarations). Reversed outputs are re-charged at the applicable Luxembourg VAT rate (16% standard headline, or the reduced rate if the goods are diverted to domestic or EU consumption), with monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% per month and administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 per infraction for defective invoicing, books, or declarations. Intentional or fraudulent export arrangements, including carrousel or missing-trader fraud, trigger criminal prosecution (imprisonment and fines), joint and several liability of directors, refusal of refund claims, customs penalties under the Code des douanes, and publicity measures in egregious cases; managers cannot invoke the foreign customer's payment default or delivery instructions to excuse an unsubstantiated zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and AML supervision; cross-border statistical reporting is administered by the BCL under EU Balance of Payments Regulation and Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current account and capital account operations within the framework of the EU Treaty and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Luxembourg imposes no general exchange control restrictions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, repayment of shareholder loans, and liquidation proceeds to non-resident shareholders proceed freely without prior regulatory authorisation, subject to documentation requirements imposed by the bank under AML/CFT legislation and the BCL balance-of-payments reporting threshold of EUR 12,500 per transaction. As the entity operates a physical grocery store selling imported Asian products, all trade-related settlements in EUR or foreign currency are unrestricted; no differentiated approval is required for merchants or retailers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender rules exist in Luxembourg. Resident entities are not required to convert or repatriate foreign-currency export proceeds within any statutory timeline. Foreign-currency earnings may be retained in bank accounts indefinitely. For statistical compliance, export receipts exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction must be reported to the Banque Centrale du Luxembourg through the monthly BCL balance-of-payments reporting system; no conversion ratio applies and no exchange approval is needed for remittances abroad.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account (bloque / séquestre) for initial share capital deposit prior to notarial act; operational EUR current account with international payment services and supplier credit lines.
Capital escrow account / corporate transaction account with SEPA and SWIFT MT103/MT700 capabilities and dedicated retail merchant acquiring.
Commercial operating account with multi-currency functionalities, treasury and FX hedging services for mid-cap and retail trade companies.
Daily operational EUR account and term deposit account; retail POS acquiring and e-commerce settlement accounts.
Corporate current account and documentary credit facilities; trade finance account for import settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low for the primary operational account, due to the statutory retail POS acquiring and cash handling requirements. A Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institution (under CSSF) or an EU/EEA EMI passporting into Luxembourg can legally provide e-money accounts for cross-border supplier payments; however, an offshore/digital EMI established outside the EU/EEA has no direct access to Luxembourg domestic payment rails, point-of-sale acquiring, or intra-eurozone settlement without a licensed correspondent intermediary. For this grocery retail model, an EMI is viable only as an auxiliary treasury tool for settling imports from Asian suppliers in USD or CNY, not as the principal clearing bank. Legal constraints under PSD2, the Settlement Finality Law, and CSSF Circulars restrict deposit-taking and require safeguarding of funds. The overall feasibility rating is 'medium' with a clear carve-out for supplier disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SARL typical of the low-risk grocery retail sector, at least one authorised director or beneficial owner must attend a physical interview at a Luxembourg branch or, alternatively, complete an interactive video-identification session using an eIDAS-qualified remote onboarding tool where the bank’s internal policy permits. Most incumbent Tier-1 banks require the final identity verification and ultimate beneficial owner declaration (RBE) to be authenticated by a Luxembourg-based professional or notarised power of attorney. Remote opening is possible if the bank applies an equivalent level of assurance to the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive, but the commercial reality is that for non-resident directors from high-risk Asian jurisdictions, a physical presence in Luxembourg during the bank onboarding interview significantly improves acceptance speed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived absence of economic substance (shell company risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete substance dossier: notarised articles of association of the SARL, current certificate of registration with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS), a signed commercial lease in Luxembourg for the grocery hub, payroll and social security declarations evidencing local employees, audited or certified annual accounts, board meeting minutes showing decisions in Luxembourg, VAT and income tax registrations, and a transparent group structure diagram with ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate cash-intensive retail turnover with limited cash management documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statistical details from the registered POS system, daily till reconciliation and cash management policy, documented weekly cash deposits with the bank, inventory and supplier invoice records, turnover declarations for VAT and corporate income tax, and insurance certificates covering stock and cash-in-transit arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections to the SARL from shareholders located in high-risk Asian jurisdictions or with high net wealth unexplained by income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidentiary package: notarised capital increase deeds, bank and brokerage statements, notarised share purchase agreements, tax residence certificates and tax returns, certification from the foreign corporate registry, ultimate beneficial owner register declarations, AML questionnaires, and any independent legal opinion validating the origin of the injected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outward trade payments to suppliers of Asian food products without clear bilateral trade documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Import documentation suite: EU Single Administrative Document (SAD) customs declarations, ATR or EUR.1 certificates for preferential origin claims, bills of lading / airway bills, purchase orders, supplier invoices, conformity declarations for foodstuff imports (including CVED for animal-origin products), health certificates, and evidence that the goods physically enter the Luxembourg/EU customs territory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the parent company or shareholders must be routed through the banking system using a SWIFT MT103 message (or SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR). The remitter bank must include the correct EU Balance of Payments purpose code — for direct investment equity capital, code A.1.1 (ordinary shares) or A.1.2 (other equity / partnership interest), and the payment reference should clearly state 'Capital increase – Libraire / SARL Luxembourg'. The receiving Luxembourg bank will require the notarial deed of capital increase (procès-verbal) and the updated RCS filing to reconcile the account credit. The BCL monthly balance-of-payments reporting obligation applies automatically to all cross-border flows in excess of EUR 12,500. No exchange-control licence is required. If the injection takes the form of a shareholder loan, the purpose code A.1.3 (loans to resident by non-resident) should be used, with a loan agreement and transfer-pricing justification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of supplier invoices for imported Asian groceries, the principal rails are: (i) direct SWIFT MT103 high-value or standard-value credits for USD/CNY/JPY and other non-EUR currencies; (ii) SEPA instant or SEPA credit transfer for EUR-denominated EU supplier payments; (iii) documentary letters of credit opened through a Luxembourg commercial bank (SWIFT MT700 issue, MT710 advice, MT400 reimbursement) when transacting with Asian banks requiring LC security. For daily low-value disbursements to local service providers, the Luxembourg domestic clearing system uses TARGET2 for large-value and STEP/SEPA for retail. Bank charges are typically split; the SARL’s contracts should clearly designate payment terms (e.g., 70% documents and 30% advance). In all cases, the bank mandate must pre-set the purpose code C.2.1 (imports of goods) and include scanned invoices and customs declarations in the compliance workflow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards traded with a licensed Luxembourg/EEA bank under standard ISDA or local FX master agreement, with maturities typically up to 12 months and delivery in USD/CNY/JPY/EUR;

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with transferability restrictions, especially CNY (onshore/settlement offshore) and certain Southeast Asian currencies, transacted with licensed global banks in Luxembourg;
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps) for long-term supply-chain financing or shareholder-loan currency risk management, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement;

Foreign-exchange options (zero-cost collars, call/put spreads) for protecting import payment cash flows against adverse USD/EUR and CNY/EUR moves, subject to internal derivative governance and CSSF EMIR documentation requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholders' approval of the annual accounts and in any event no later than seven months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 July of the following fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to court-imposed civil fines under the amended Law of 19 December 2002; persistent default may result in mandatory court-ordered filing, daily penalty payments, and eventual administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the month of the anniversary of the RBE registration; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, including share transfers that modify control or ownership thresholds, must be filed within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update the UBO declaration constitutes a criminal offence under the Law of 13 January 2019, punishable by fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per violation; intentional concealment may lead to higher fines and imprisonment, and the company may be barred from making distributions until compliance is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate direct tax return, including corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is due before 30 June of the year following the relevant tax year; the Luxembourg tax office may grant an extension upon formal request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers late-filing penalties, default tax assessments, and statutory interest on unpaid taxes; the ACD may enforce recovery by seizure of bank accounts and other assets. Repeated non-compliance can contribute to an administrative declaration of the company as non-compliant and strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SARL is subject to statutory independent audit when, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds more than one of the following thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, or an average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also required for public-interest entities or when imposed by provisions in the articles of association.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted or required only for consolidated financial statements and certain qualifying group structures, not for a standalone SARL grocery business.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership information with the Luxembourg RBE during the anniversary month of the initial registration. Any shareholding transfer or change in ownership resulting in a new ultimate beneficial owner must be reported within one month of the transaction; the reporting threshold is 25% ownership, voting rights, or equivalent control.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $10,000 - $25,000 per annum for a small grocery SARL statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate rate: 17.00% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge [7% of CIT] + 6.75% municipal business tax; 15.00% CIT applies on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income)
